Back Pain Should Never Be Ignored – It May Be a Warning Sign of Spine TB

A young patient from Byculla, Mumbai, initially came to me with only back pain. Since there were no major neurological symptoms at first, he was started on medicines and kept under close observation with regular follow-up. For a few weeks he was doing well, but then he stopped coming for follow-up.

After some time, he suddenly called me with imbalance while walking for 5 days and difficulty passing urine. I immediately advised admission. On examination, he had already started developing weakness in both lower limbs. An urgent MRI spine showed spinal TB with epidural collection causing compression of the spinal cord in the lumbar region.

This was a neurosurgical emergency. He was taken up for urgent surgery, the pressure on the spinal cord was relieved, and thankfully he had an excellent post-operative recovery with complete regain of power in both legs.

This case highlights an important message: never ignore persistent back pain, especially if it worsens or is associated with walking imbalance, leg weakness, or urinary difficulty. In conditions like Koch’s spine / spinal TB, delayed treatment can lead to permanent nerve damage or paralysis. Timely diagnosis, regular follow-up, and early surgical intervention when needed can result in full recovery.

If you are suffering from back pain, spine infection, spinal TB, leg weakness, or nerve compression, consult Dr. Bhushan Meshram, Neurosurgeon.

Young Professionals & IT Employees: Don’t Ignore Neck Pain – It May Be a New Occupational Hazard

In today’s digital world, neck pain in the young generation is becoming increasingly common, especially among people working long hours in IT jobs, desk jobs, and computer-based professions. Prolonged sitting, poor posture, continuous laptop use, and lack of movement are turning neck pain into a new occupational hazard.

Common symptoms include neck stiffness, pain radiating to the shoulders or arms, tingling or numbness in the hands, headaches, and even weakness in the arms. If ignored, these problems may lead to cervical disc prolapse, nerve compression, or cervical spondylosis at a young age.

How to prevent neck pain:
✔ Maintain correct sitting posture
✔ Keep your screen at eye level
✔ Use an ergonomic chair and proper back support
✔ Take short breaks every 30–40 minutes
✔ Do regular neck stretching and strengthening exercises
✔ Avoid prolonged mobile/laptop bending posture

When should you see a neurosurgeon?
If your neck pain is persistent, severe, associated with arm pain, tingling, numbness, weakness, imbalance while walking, or is not improving with rest and physiotherapy, timely consultation is important.

Dr. Bhushan Meshram, Neurosurgeon, offers expert evaluation and treatment for neck pain, cervical spine problems, slipped disc, and nerve compression. Early diagnosis can prevent long-term complications.

Traumatic Head Injury: Recognize the Symptoms and Seek Timely Treatment

A traumatic head injury can occur due to road traffic accidents, falls at home, sports injuries, workplace accidents, or physical trauma. While some head injuries may appear minor initially, they can lead to serious complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly.

Common Symptoms of Head Injury:
✅ Loss of consciousness
✅ Persistent headache
✅ Vomiting or nausea
✅ Drowsiness or confusion
✅ Memory loss
✅ Seizures (fits)
✅ Weakness of arms or legs
✅ Difficulty speaking or walking
✅ Bleeding from the nose or ears

A severe head injury can cause bleeding inside the brain (brain hemorrhage), skull fractures, brain swelling, or life-threatening pressure on the brain. Immediate medical evaluation with a CT scan is often essential to identify these conditions.

Management of Traumatic Brain Injury
Treatment depends on the severity of the injury. Mild cases may require observation and medications, while serious cases may need emergency neurosurgical intervention such as removal of blood clots, decompression surgery, or intensive neurocritical care.

Early diagnosis and timely treatment significantly improve outcomes and can prevent permanent neurological damage.

If you or your loved one experiences symptoms following a head injury, seek urgent neurosurgical consultation.

Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH): A Treatable Cause of Memory Loss and Walking Difficulty

Many elderly patients experience difficulty walking, forgetfulness, and loss of bladder control, often assuming it is a normal part of aging. However, these symptoms may be due to Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH), a condition caused by excess cerebrospinal fluid accumulating in the brain.

The classic symptoms of NPH include:
✔ Difficulty walking or imbalance while walking
✔ Memory problems or confusion
✔ Urinary urgency or loss of bladder control

The good news is that Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus is one of the few reversible causes of dementia-like symptoms. Early diagnosis with brain imaging and proper neurological evaluation can make a significant difference.

If identified and treated in time, many patients can experience remarkable improvement in walking, memory, and daily activities. Treatment usually involves the placement of a ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt, which helps drain excess fluid from the brain.

Awareness is crucial. If you or your loved one has developed unexplained gait imbalance, memory decline, or urinary symptoms, do not ignore these warning signs. Timely consultation with an experienced neurosurgeon can help achieve excellent outcomes and even complete recovery in suitable cases.

World Brain Tumor Day: Early Diagnosis Can Save Lives

On World Brain Tumor Day, it is important to spread awareness about brain tumors, their symptoms, and the available treatment options.

A brain tumor is an abnormal growth of cells within the brain. Brain tumors can be benign (non-cancerous) or malignant (cancerous). Common types include meningioma, glioma, pituitary tumors, acoustic neuroma, metastatic brain tumors, and pediatric brain tumors.

Symptoms of a Brain Tumor
✔ Persistent headaches, especially in the morning
✔ Seizures or fits
✔ Weakness in the arms or legs
✔ Difficulty in speech or memory
✔ Imbalance while walking
✔ Blurred or double vision
✔ Personality or behavioral changes

Treatment Options
Treatment depends on the type, size, and location of the tumor and may include:
• Advanced microsurgical brain tumor removal
• Endoscopic brain surgery
• Radiation therapy
• Chemotherapy
• Targeted and multidisciplinary treatments

Early diagnosis and timely treatment can significantly improve outcomes and quality of life.

Neck Pain, Hand Weakness & Imbalance While Walking? It Could Be OPLL (Ossified Posterior Longitudinal Ligament)

A 56-year-old gentleman visited our clinic with severe neck pain radiating to both arms, tingling and numbness in his hands, difficulty holding objects, and increasing imbalance while walking.

On examination, he was found to have cervical myelopathy, a serious condition caused by pressure on the spinal cord. His MRI revealed Ossified Posterior Longitudinal Ligament (OPLL) causing severe cervical spinal cord compression along with myelomalacia (damage to the spinal cord).

Considering the progressive neurological symptoms, he underwent cervical laminectomy with cervical spine fusion surgery. The results were encouraging—his hand grip improved immediately after surgery. With dedicated physiotherapy, his walking balance gradually improved, and within two months he regained independence in his daily activities.

This case highlights the importance of early diagnosis and timely surgical intervention in OPLL and cervical myelopathy. Delaying treatment can lead to permanent nerve damage, severe disability, or even paralysis.

Persistent Headache in a Teenager Turned Out to Be Arnold Chiari Malformation

A 15-year-old girl visited my clinic with a history of severe headaches for the last 2 years. The pain typically started at the back of the neck and radiated to the forehead. She had been treated as a migraine patient by multiple doctors, but her symptoms continued.

During a detailed consultation, one symptom stood out—intermittent numbness in her left arm. A thorough neurological examination revealed subtle weakness in her left hand, which she had ignored because she was right-hand dominant. Her reflexes were exaggerated, suggesting an underlying neurological problem. On further questioning, she also reported imbalance while walking, especially on uneven surfaces.

An urgent MRI brain and cervical spine confirmed Arnold Chiari Malformation, a condition where the cerebellar tonsils descend through the foramen magnum, causing compression of the brainstem and spinal cord.

She underwent Foramen Magnum Decompression Surgery the following week and made an excellent recovery, being discharged within 5 days.

This case highlights the importance of meticulous history taking and neurological examination. Not every headache is migraine. Persistent headaches associated with numbness, weakness, balance issues, or neurological symptoms should never be ignored, especially in young adults and children.

Kyphoplasty and Nerve Root Block: Avoiding Major Spine Surgery in Elderly Patients

A 65-year-old lady came to me with severe back and leg pain that had returned just one month after undergoing lumbar fusion surgery (L4-S1) elsewhere. Over the next few months, her symptoms worsened, making walking and daily activities difficult.

After taking a detailed history, performing a thorough neurological examination, and carefully reviewing all her scans, I found that the source of her pain had been missed. Her leg pain was due to compression of the L5 nerve root, while her severe back pain was caused by an osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture that had not been identified during the previous surgery.

Considering her age, diabetes, and hypertension, a major revision spine surgery with a longer fusion would have involved a large incision, prolonged recovery, and higher surgical risks.

Instead, I offered a minimally invasive solution: L5 nerve root block and Kyphoplasty, both performed under local anesthesia through tiny needle punctures without any major cuts.

The procedure was successful. Her back and leg pain improved dramatically, she was able to walk comfortably, and she was discharged the very next day.

This case highlights how Kyphoplasty for osteoporotic spine fractures and targeted nerve root injections can provide excellent pain relief and functional recovery in carefully selected patients, often avoiding the need for extensive revision spine surgery.

Safe Brain Tumor Surgery Near the Motor Cortex with Neuromonitoring

Advanced Neuromonitoring Helps Preserve Brain Function During Brain Tumor Surgery

A 70-year-old gentleman came to us with gradually worsening weakness of the left hand and leg. His relatives noticed difficulty in walking and reduced strength on the left side, following which an MRI brain scan revealed a large right-sided brain tumor. The tumor was located dangerously close to the motor cortex — the vital area of the brain that controls body movements.

I explained to the family that surgery was necessary, but because the tumor was very close to the nerve fibres controlling movement, there was a significant risk of paralysis. To improve safety, we planned the surgery with advanced intraoperative neuromonitoring.

Neuromonitoring during brain tumor surgery helps identify and protect critical brain pathways in real time. It allows precise tumor excision while preserving important neurological function and minimizing the risk of permanent weakness or paralysis.

The surgery lasted nearly 4 hours. The patient stayed in the ICU for one day and recovered remarkably well. The brain tumor was completely excised, and most importantly, he had no paralysis after surgery.

Considering her age and comorbidities, I discussed the option of vertebroplasty, a minimally invasive spine procedure where medical cement is injected into the fractured vertebra to stabilize the bone and relieve pain. I explained that the procedure could be performed under awake local anesthesia, avoiding the risks of major surgery.

She underwent vertebroplasty and the transformation was remarkable. By the same evening, she was able to walk pain-free. The relief on her face and happiness of her family reminded us how timely treatment can restore independence and quality of life.

Lumbar spinal stenosis is a condition that occurs when the spaces within the lower spine become narrower, which may place pressure on nearby nerves. This condition is more commonly seen with age-related changes in the spine, although other factors may also contribute to its development.

Common symptoms can include lower back pain, leg pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness, particularly during walking or prolonged standing. The severity of symptoms can vary from person to person, and not everyone with lumbar spinal stenosis experiences the same challenges.
